OPENS Ch 20 — HOMILETIC-GENRE ANCHOR (per source-fidelity note): post-resurrection-cycle homiletic + martyr-cult formation. The chapter's likely thematic-content: in the narrative-progression after the first martyrdom-cycle (Chs 3-4) and the homiletic-instruction (Chs 5-7 + 8-19), Ch 20 likely transitions to MARTYR-CULT formation themes — the institutional-memorialization of the Maqabean-martyrs. Parallels: 4 MACCABEES 17:8-22 (Maccabean-martyrs' monumentalization + the inscription-of-virtue); 2 MACCABEES 7:38 + 8:1-7 (Judas Maccabeus's vow + revolt-following the martyrdoms); HEBREWS 11:35 (the 'others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection' — read as Maccabean-martyr reference in patristic tradition); MARTYRDOM OF POLYCARP 18 (the martyr-cult's anniversary celebrations); CYPRIAN Epistle 22 (memorial-mass for the martyrs). Tewahedo Sǝnkǝsar (Synaxarium) preserves the Maccabean-martyrs' feast-day commemoration (1 August in EOTC calendar) drawing on this chapter's likely martyr-cult institution-narrative.

TIER-2 AUDIT INTEGRATION (γ.4.8.F) — SENKESSAR ABIJĀ/SILĀ SAINT-DATES ROUTE PRECISE. Per TIER2_AUDIT.md §4, the standard reference for the Ethiopian-Synaxarium Abijā/Silä saint-day claim (Horovitz 1905 p. 195, citing Hiob Ludolf) is **E. A. Wallis Budge, *The Book of the Saints of the Ethiopian Church: A Translation of the Ethiopic Synaxarium (Mäṣḥafä Sǝnkǝssar)*, 4 vols. (Cambridge University Press, 1928)** — made from British Museum manuscripts Oriental 660 and 661. Public domain on archive.org (`bookofsaintsofet00yait` and `bookofsaintsofet0001unse`). Volume 2 covers months **Ṭǝr through Miyazya**; the Abijā/Silä entries are at **Ṭǝr 21** and **Ṭǝr 30** — ETHIOPIAN-CALENDAR DATES corresponding to roughly **29 January and 7 February** in the modern Gregorian calendar. Ludolf, writing in the 17th century, gave the Ethiopian month-name in the older loose-equivalence form 'January 21/30' — these are NOT Gregorian January 21 + 30. The route is now precise; final confirmation of the Synaxarium's specific Abijā/Silä description and Maccabean-martyr linkage awaits direct reading of Budge vol. 2. The chapter's martyr-cult-formation theme (γ.4.8.E 20:1 entry) is grounded in this Synaxarium feast-day tradition.
